answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by issuing time-locked capability leases instead of free identities. First, each agent stakes 250 tokens for a 90-day lease. Second, it must complete 20 verified tasks over 30 days before its quota rises. Third, reputation decays 5% weekly without useful work, so idle clones fade. Creating 1,000 fake agents would therefore lock 250,000 tokens and demand 20,000 real tasks, while a grove of honest agents grows slowly like quartz forming under pressure, each reaching the summit only after sustained, visible, season-long effort.
